key_insight: PrivMeSA lets a local clinical agent decide when to consult remote LLMs while learning to minimize patient data exposure across multi-turn conversations.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinical AI systems get expert help without leaking identifiable patient information, especially in settings with repeated encounters.
method: Local agent handles each encounter and negotiates with remote specialist models.
Reinforcement learning balances task accuracy against disclosure and registry-based re-identification risk over the full outbound transcript.
A local lesson memory turns completed consultations into reusable guidance, reducing future remote queries.
evidence_signal: On an emergency-department benchmark built from MIMIC-IV-ED records, it improved mean task accuracy by up to 15.8 points and reduced personal-detail disclosure from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases.
watch_item: Privacy gains depend on the registry-based risk setup and local memory design, so real-world deployment still needs validation across sites, workflows, and evolving privacy threats.
paper_title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
